modelReview.summary: The study is an unbound exploratory prediction evaluation lacking protocol, variable definitions, model description, calibration, sample size justification, and missing data analysis. It cannot be interpreted as a confirmatory finding.

findings.title: Analysis is explicitly unbound and lacks pre‑registration
findings.whyItMatters: Without a pre‑specified analysis plan, all results become exploratory and cannot support confirmatory claims. The binding status ‘unbound’ and result posture ‘exploratory_standard_table’ indicate that no protocol or AnalysisSpec governs this run.
findings.actionableFix: Create a pre‑registered protocol or analysis specification, bind the statistical run to it, and re‑run the analysis before submitting as a final manuscript.

findings.title: Outcome, exposure and covariates are not defined
findings.whyItMatters: Readers cannot reproduce the study or interpret the clinical meaning of the prediction. Only generic names ‘outcome_binary’ and ‘pred_score’ appear, with no operational definitions.
findings.actionableFix: Provide a complete data dictionary with definitions, measurement scales, and derivation rules for every variable used.

findings.title: Origin and nature of the prediction model are undisclosed
findings.whyItMatters: The model that generated ‘pred_score’ is not described (e.g., logistic regression, random forest, external risk score). Reproducibility and internal validity cannot be assessed, and overfitting or data leakage cannot be ruled out.
findings.actionableFix: Describe the model class, training data, feature set, hyperparameters, and any internal validation (e.g., cross‑validation) that produced the predicted probabilities.

findings.title: No calibration assessment performed
findings.whyItMatters: For risk prediction, good discrimination (AUROC) does not imply good calibration. Without calibration intercept, slope, or calibration plot, the model may give misleadingly over‑ or under‑confident predictions.
findings.actionableFix: Add calibration‑in‑the‑large, calibration slope, a calibration plot, and optionally a decision curve analysis.

findings.title: Sample size is small with no justification or event rate reported
findings.whyItMatters: Prediction model evaluation requires adequate events per candidate predictor. Without the event rate or a sample‑size justification, the study may be severely underpowered or produce unstable estimates.
findings.actionableFix: Report the outcome prevalence (number of events), discuss event‑per‑variable criteria, or provide a sample size calculation justifying the current N.

findings.title: No missing‑data analysis beyond a complete‑case statement
findings.whyItMatters: Complete‑case analysis can bias evaluation if missingness is related to outcome or predictors. The study provides no flow chart, comparison of excluded vs included subjects, or sensitivity analysis.
findings.actionableFix: Describe the initial sample, record‑level exclusions, and compare demographics of included and excluded records. Consider multiple imputation or a missing‑at‑random sensitivity analysis.

findings.title: Manuscript is presented as final while self‑documented as exploratory and unreviewed
evidenceRefs: manuscript.md#/What This Does And Does Not Show
findings.whyItMatters: The paper admits it is not bound to an analysis plan, lacks a reader‑facing report, and has unaddressed advisory issues. Submitting it as a final manuscript is premature and may mislead stakeholders.
findings.actionableFix: Downgrade the manuscript to an exploratory technical note, resolve all flagged issues, and undergo proper protocol‑governed analysis before resubmitting.

missingEvidence: Model training details (algorithm, features, internal validation)
Sample size justification or event rate
Missing‑data flow chart and sensitivity analysis
